newsitem.title: UK: Quarter of a million UK homes switch gas supply.
newsitem.headline: Quarter of a million UK homes switch gas supply.

text.p: Nearly 250,000 British domestic gas users have switched supplier since deregulation started last April in a limited pilot area, energy minister Lord Fraser said on Thursday.
From Friday, a new area comprising Kent and East and West Sussex in southeast England opens to competition, and already 100,000 consumers there have signed up for new suppliers, Fraser said.

"Nearly a million gas consumers in Kent and Sussex will be able to cut an average 65 stg or more from their gas bills - and over 100,000 consumers there have already signed up for new suppliers," Fraser said.
He added that with those who have already changed suppliers in the southwest, "this brings to nearly 250,000 the number who have now decided that gas competition is good for them."
Of those 250,000, 120,000 already receive gas from new suppliers while the remainder are entered into a computer system and will start receiving gas from new suppliers within two weeks.

Domestic competition in gas supply is being phased in gradually. Last April, a first pilot area covering 500,000 customers in Devon, Cornwall and Somerset was the first to open up. Until then, only British Gas plc, now demerged into Centrica plc and BG plc could supply domestic consumers.
This was then extended to Dorset and Avon on February 10. And with competition starting in Kent and East and West Sussex on Friday, over two million households are now eligible to switch supplier.
"Reaching the two million milestone means that full competition...is no longer a pilot project but a practical benefit," Fraser said.

Full domestic competition across Britain is due to start next year, and Fraser added that he was in discussion with Clare Spottiswoode, Director General of Gas Supply, on "just what our options are for bringing competition quickly to the rest of the country."
